provenance.source: Saudi Social Insurance Law (GOSI); PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Saudi Arabia - Individual - Other taxes
provenance.notes: Confirmed on 31 August 2026 that Saudi Arabia levies no income tax on employment income, and that GOSI applies to Saudi nationals at 9.75% employee share with a SAR 45,000 monthly ceiling. Non-Saudi employees make no contribution; their employer pays 2% occupational hazard cover.

omissions: GOSI is charged on basic salary plus housing allowance. This app applies it to whatever you enter as monthly pay, which will overstate it if you enter total remuneration.
End-of-service benefits are a contractual entitlement, not a tax, and are not modelled.
The new pension rules for employees who joined the scheme after July 2024 phase in different rates and are not modelled.

personalIncomeTax.legalRef: There is no personal income tax on employment income in Saudi Arabia.
personalIncomeTax.note: Saudi Arabia levies no income tax on wages, for nationals or expatriates. Zakat and corporate income tax apply to businesses, not to employees.

socialInsurance.note: The Saudi employee pays 9% pension plus 0.75% SANED unemployment cover, on basic salary plus housing, up to SAR 45,000 a month. A non-Saudi employee pays nothing; the employer alone pays 2% for occupational hazard cover.

regions.name: Saudi Arabia
regions.note: No regional variation in either tax or contributions.

inputSchema.label: Basic salary plus housing (per month)
inputSchema.help: GOSI is charged on basic salary plus housing allowance, not on total remuneration. Enter that figure rather than your full package, or the contribution shown will be too high.

inputSchema.label: Status
inputSchema.help: GOSI social insurance is compulsory for Saudi nationals only. An expatriate employee pays neither income tax nor social insurance, so gross pay is take-home pay.
